correctness.rationale: The primitive period \(p=b+d+2\) has distinct length-\(p\) phase signatures because unequal zero gaps exclude proper powers. At \(n>p\), the first p symbols of each successive cyclic shift force advancing phases and hence \(p\mid n\). For \(n<p\), factor zeros number at most two. All-one words, one-zero words with the interval-cover criterion \(j\le\min(d,2b+1)\), and one possible two-zero class \((01^b)^2\) exhaust the cases. The full formula and GF follow, and a monotone two-branch calculation gives the sharp period-mass bound and all equality cases. Actual standalone verifier compared complete conjugacy-class sets at 28,766 \((b,d,n)\) cases and exact extremal census for \(5\le p\le99\); these finite cases are corroboration only. The proof separately treats \(n=1\), \(n=p\) and \(n>p\), and excludes \(b=d\) explicitly.

value.rationale: Two unequal zero-to-zero return gaps are the simplest nontrivial primitive binary periodic marker system, and all-conjugate factor presence is the established Lie complexity invariant. The result provides every actual class for every factor length, separates transient classes from the permanent primitive-period multiples, identifies the sharp 3-class threshold and all fixed-period maximizers of the natural first-period mass. Its combination of full structural classification and sharp optimizer analysis is meaningful beyond brute-force enumeration; no broad theory or downstream theorem is claimed.
